brief: BofA reads the released August CPI as clearing the way for a Fed hike next week. Headline rose 0.4% m/m, in line, while core was firmer at 0.3% (0.29% unrounded). The note says the core y/y rate was unchanged at 3.4%, though its own y/y table prints core at 2.45%. The detail lifted BofA's August core PCE tracking estimate from 0.26% to 0.30% m/m, and set against market pricing of 21bp for next week's FOMC, BofA says the report should greenlight a hike. It takes little trend signal from the print: core services rose 0.33%, wireless telephone services jumped 5.9% for roughly 10bp of core on AT&T retiring some unlimited plans and raising fees, and airfares plus lodging added 8bp, effects BofA expects to unwind. Chairman Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks and market pricing raised the cost of disappointing, and renewed twist flattening gives him a credibility argument. September hike pricing rose to about 85%, and the long end rallied entirely through real yields, supporting BofA's long-held real-yield flattener. Not hiking would risk a long-end selloff larger than the post-July FOMC move. The dollar retraced an initial rally. BofA expects further hikes in October and December unless data soften.
